clue.text: Nothing good is postponed

parts.note: nought, the zero-shaped letter
pleasant, agreeable

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that nothing good ever happens on schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans put on ice are shelved or deferred, an idiom for suspension until later.

clue.text: Company from the south — one charged to hold up employment

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading from the south means reading bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: standard abbreviation for company

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it within, so the charged particle wraps round the next word

parts.note: a cation is a positively charged ion
taken as written

explanation.surface: A firm in the south has someone indicted for robbery holding up its jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One charged' suggests a criminal suspect, but it is a chemistry term; the up goes after its first letter: C-UP-ATION.
explanation.definitionFit: An occupation is a job or profession, the work by which someone earns a living.

clue.text: Little mischief? One's played quietly

parts.note: 'one's' read as 'I am', contracted to I'M
P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: A child gets up to a small prank, then plays without making a sound.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as playful: the answer is a little mischief-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: An imp is a small mischievous sprite, or a naughty child, a personified bit of mischief.

clue.text: Aim to secure right artist for commission

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast inside, so the word for aim encloses the following letters

parts.note: an end is a goal or purpose
standard abbreviation for right
RA, Royal Academician

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to sign up the ideal painter for a commissioned work.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an art commission; the definition means a task one is sent to do.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand is a short trip or task carried out on someone's behalf, a small commission.

clue.text: Car — blue — drawing in constant power from only one source?

indicators.note: to draw something in is to pull it inside, so the joined car and blue words take a letter into their middle

parts.note: short for automobile
blue as in risqué or smutty
C is the standard symbol for a constant, e.g. the speed of light

explanation.surface: A puzzling description of a blue car that runs on electricity from a single supply.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like an electric car drawing current; the question mark flags that 'power' means political rule.
explanation.definitionFit: An autocracy is government by a single absolute ruler, so all political authority flows from one person.

clue.text: Lovely candy decoration on top of lebkuchen

parts.note: angelica is candied plant stem used to decorate cakes

indicators.note: the top of a down-reading word is its first letter, so only the initial of the German biscuit counts

parts.note: the first letter of lebkuchen

explanation.surface: A pretty sugared garnish sits on top of a German gingerbread.
explanation.walkthrough: Lebkuchen are German spiced honey biscuits; in a down entry the candied stem sits above the initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelical means like an angel, hence beautiful and sweet, a poetic word for lovely.

clue.text: Otter that regularly eats river fish

indicators.note: something that eats takes food inside itself, so the kept letters swallow the river symbol
regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter of the first words is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters
standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An otter routinely feeds on fish from the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetra is a small brightly coloured tropical freshwater fish, popular in aquariums.

clue.text: Hours in transit leading to former trading hub

indicators.note: in places the hours symbol within the word for transit

parts.note: cartage is the transport of goods by cart
H is the abbreviation for hours

explanation.surface: Time spent on the road on the way to an ancient port city.
explanation.definitionFit: Carthage was the ancient Phoenician city in North Africa that dominated Mediterranean commerce until Rome destroyed it.

clue.text: A lad arrives furiously combative

indicators.note: acting furiously means in a wild rage, so the letters before it are tossed about

parts.note: all eleven letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young man turns up in a rage, spoiling for a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Adversarial describes an approach based on opposition or conflict, hostile and confrontational.

clue.text: Not large, really flipping basic dwelling

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the remaining letters are read backwards
not here means without, so the letter for large is left out

parts.note: truly means really
standard abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A small, simple, crude little shack, described with a mild expletive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British swear word intensifying 'basic'; it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A yurt is a circular felt-covered tent used by Central Asian nomads, a simple portable home.

clue.text: Officer requires years just to get protection for work

parts.note: a police officer
standard abbreviation for years
just in the sense of fair or correct

explanation.surface: A police officer needs only a few years' service to earn job security.
explanation.definitionFit: Copyright is the legal right protecting an author's or artist's creative output from being copied.

clue.text: Partygoer close to dancefloor, say

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter of the following word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of dancefloor
to aver is to state or declare

explanation.surface: A clubber hangs around near the dancefloor, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' reads as 'near' in the surface but here means the end letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A raver is someone who attends lively all-night dance parties or raves.

clue.text: Shelter covered with light, rocky earth and shiny material

indicators.note: a thing covered with something else sits inside it, so the shelter goes within the word for light

parts.note: light in colour, pale
a tent is a simple shelter

indicators.note: rocky suggests unsteady and shaken up, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

parts.note: its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lean-to with a light covering on rocky ground, plus some glossy fabric, sounds like a camping kit list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shelter' opens the clue and looks like the definition, but the shiny material at the end is.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent leather is leather given a hard glossy lacquered finish, used for smart shoes and bags.

clue.text: Invitations gathered up at points to be dished out

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: people who gathered met

parts.note: the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Party invitations collected and then handed out at various places.
explanation.definitionFit: A temptation is an enticement, something that invites or lures one to act.

clue.text: Old male German paramilitaries overwhelmed by strength test

indicators.note: something overwhelmed is engulfed, so the paramilitaries are swallowed by the word for strength

parts.note: an asset is a strong point
SS men, members of the Nazi Schutzstaffel

explanation.surface: Former Nazi troopers are outmatched in a trial of strength.
explanation.walkthrough: The SS was the Nazi paramilitary force; 'old' places it in history and 'male' makes them men.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessment is an evaluation or examination, such as a school or medical test.

clue.text: Book publishers should send my royalties here!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a large, heavy volume

definitions.text: publishers should send my royalties here!
definitions.meaning: second meaning: an author's demand that the money come their way, split as two words

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer is what a greedy author would say about where the cheques should go.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a big scholarly volume, while the split phrase indicates direction towards the speaker.

clue.text: Singular limits restricting key attack victims

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the word for limits wraps round what follows it

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
caps are upper limits, as on spending
E is a musical key
to go at someone is to attack them

explanation.surface: Odd boundaries are set around a key assault by some victims, a jumble of military jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: Scapegoats are people made to bear the blame for others' faults, unjust victims of collective blame.

clue.text: Use moderate wordplay with sarcasm

parts.note: to use wordplay is to pun
in a moderate, mild way

explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads as an instruction: 'use wordplay' in a moderate way is PUN GENTLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Pungent remarks are sharply biting or caustic, so speaking pungently is speaking with cutting irony.

clue.text: Settled dispute outlined by contract

a fray is a fight or quarrel

explanation.walkthrough: 'Settled' suggests resolving the dispute, but it means paying a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To defray costs is to pay them, so a settled bill has been defrayed.

clue.text: Broken bone somehow compressing extremely tough joint

indicators.note: to compress is to squeeze in, so the jumbled word holds the end letters inside it
somehow means in some undetermined manner, so the word before it is rearranged

parts.note: its letters are rearranged

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only its outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of tough
a link is a joint or connection

explanation.surface: A fractured bone squashes a really stiff joint, like a medical report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' sits by 'bone' and looks like its anagram signal, but it is the definition; the later adverb does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine on the blink is faulty or not working properly, an informal idiom for being out of order.

clue.text: One advising young woman to drop married name

indicators.note: dropping something means letting it go, so the letters for married and name are taken out

parts.note: a maiden is a girl or young unmarried woman

explanation.walkthrough: Removing both M and N from MAIDEN leaves AIDE; the surface plays on a woman keeping her maiden name.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide is an assistant or adviser, often to a politician or senior official.

clue.text: Everyone featuring in the Republican party race

indicators.note: featuring in something means appearing within it, so the word for everyone goes inside the party abbreviation

parts.note: GOP, the Grand Old Party, nickname of the US Republicans
all means everyone

explanation.walkthrough: 'race' looks like an election race; it is the horse's fastest pace or a quick run.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallop is a fast run, especially of a horse at full speed, so a race.

clue.text: Desperate hunters battle to reverse fortunes

parts.note: the letters of both words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Hunters in trouble fight back so that the prey becomes the predator.

clue.text: Collector's items including many human sculptures?

indicators.note: including means containing within, so the answer sits inside the preceding pair of words

parts.note: found spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the definition: these are trunks of the body, a common subject of sculpture, in their Italian plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Torsi is a plural of torso, the human trunk, often carved as a sculpture without head or limbs.

clue.text: Somewhat elevated numbers in a spreadsheet?

parts.note: a tad means a little, somewhat

clue.text: Try to block some pain

parts.note: as in 'have you any?'

explanation.definitionFit: Agony is extreme physical or mental suffering, a severe form of pain.

clue.text: King and others worried about current counterattack

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the preceding words go round the symbol for current

clue.text: Excellent commando principally involved in each uprising

parts.note: the first letter of commando

a period of service or obligation
taken as written

clue.text: Sheep finally allowed outside a fold

parts.note: permitted
taken as written
